intro: The Philippines is an archipelago of over 7,600 islands in the western Pacific, grouped into Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao.

chapters.title: Islands and volcanoes
text: Luzon in the north and Mindanao in the south are the biggest islands. The Philippines sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, with active volcanoes like Mayon, famous for its perfect cone, and Taal, inside a lake.
The Mount Pinatubo eruption of 1991 was one of the largest of the 20th century and cooled the whole planet slightly.

chapters.title: Seas and reefs
text: Philippine waters are in the Coral Triangle, which has the richest sea life on Earth. Tubbataha Reef is a protected World Heritage site.
The country has one of the longest coastlines in the world.

chapters.title: Typhoons
text: About 20 tropical storms enter Philippine waters each year. Typhoon Haiyan in 2013 was one of the strongest storms ever to hit land and killed over 6,000 people.

keyTerms.meaning: A belt of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific.
A sea area with the most coral species on Earth.
